prediction_scored: hit: ratio 0.848 (0.779-0.924) lies inside the predicted 0.80-0.97 and the upper bound is below 1.00, so support_if is met by 0.076 on the upper bound. The causal reading is not supported by the exploratory placebo (see notes).
notes: Exploratory, written after the registered result was seen (analyses/turn_restrictions/did_explore.py): a placebo installation 12 months early gives a ratio of 0.9119 (0.8252-1.0078), so treated sites were already declining relative to later-treated sites before installation. Extending that pre-installation trend gives a trend-adjusted ratio of 1.0279 (0.8207-1.2873). The likely cause is the comparison group: DOT chooses sites after crash clusters, so treated sites are past their peak while later-treated sites in the same calendar months are still approaching theirs. The registered ratio therefore mixes any treatment effect with regression to the mean in opposite directions in the two groups. Checks fixed in did.py: 30 m radius 0.8436; cohorts avoiding March-June 2020 0.827 (0.7367-0.9284). Treated sites: 1,966 pedestrians injured or killed before, 1,706 after.

settle: A design that separates the treatment from regression to the mean: empirical Bayes before-after with a safety performance function, or a comparison group of untreated signalized intersections matched on the crash history DOT used for selection, registered before the data are read.
